english_translation: The Literary Star graciously bestows its blessing
meaning_notes: 文星 = the Wenqu/Wenxing star, the celestial deity governing literary talent and scholarly success. 睠 (juàn) = to regard with gracious favor. 貽 (yí) = to bestow, to leave as a legacy. Together: an archway blessing wishing the place and its people literary eminence. The four characters are carved in green fill on granite; read from the rightmost character leftward per traditional inscription convention.

source_image: Wooden door plaque (gold characters on black board)
script_type: Running/regular script (行楷), read left-to-right; vertical date on right
pinyin: Mǎ ruò tè kuàng chán fāng (rén chén nián)
english_translation: Ma-Ruo-Te Kuang Chan Meditation Hall, erected in the Ren-Chen year
meaning_notes: A named Chan (Zen) Buddhist hall or studio. 馬若特 appears to be a proper name (likely the donor, founder, or monk). 況禪坊 = "Kuang Chan Workshop/Hall." 壬辰年 is a sexagenary cyclical year (e.g., 2012 CE, 1952 CE). The plaque hangs above a dark wooden door in a traditional Chinese building, with a no-smoking sticker below indicating it is a modern heritage site.

source_image: Stone pillar vertical couplet (green calligraphy on granite)
original_traditional: 橘燈夜讀桃李春風入勝秋色
simplified_chinese: 橘灯夜读桃李春风入胜秋色
pinyin: Jú dēng yè dú táo lǐ chūn fēng rù shèng qiū sè
english_translation: By tangerine lamp at night, reading of peach and plum; spring breeze enters the splendor of autumn scenery
meaning_notes: 橘燈夜讀 alludes to the classical image of diligent study by a tangerine-peel lamp. 桃李 (peach and plum) is a metaphor for students/disciples ("through your teaching, your students flourish"). 入勝 = entering a beautiful, transcendent realm (from the idiom 引人入勝). The line merges the scholarship of night study with the lush imagery of spring peach/plum blossoms and autumn scenery. This is one half of a pillar couplet; the matching opposite pillar would bear the complementary line.

original_traditional: 子華使於齊，冉子爲其母請粟。子曰：「與之釜。」請益，曰：「與之庾。」冉子與之粟五秉。子曰：「赤之適齊也，乘肥馬，衣輕裘；吾聞之也：君子周急不繼富。」原思爲之宰，與之粟九百，辭。子曰：「毋！以與爾鄰里鄉黨乎！」
simplified_chinese: 子华使于齐，冉子为其母请粟。子曰：“与之釜。”请益，曰：“与之庾。”冉子与之粟五秉。子曰：“赤之适齐也，乘肥马，衣轻裘；吾闻之也：君子周急不继富。”原思为之宰，与之粟九百，辞。子曰：“毋！以与尔邻里乡党乎！”
pinyin: Zǐ Huá shǐ yú Qí, Rǎn zǐ wèi qí mǔ qǐng sù. Zǐ yuē: "Yǔ zhī fǔ." Qǐng yì, yuē: "Yǔ zhī yǔ." Rǎn zǐ yǔ zhī sù wǔ bǐng. Zǐ yuē: "Chì zhī shì Qí yě, chéng féi mǎ, yì qīng qiú; wú wén zhī yě: jūn zǐ zhōu jí bù jì fù." Yuán Sī wéi zhī zǎi, yǔ zhī sù jiǔ bǎi, cí. Zǐ yuē: "Wú! Yǐ yǔ ěr lín lǐ xiāng dǎng hū!"
english_translation: When Zihua (Gongxi Chi) was sent on a mission to Qi, Ran You asked Confucius for grain on behalf of Zihua's mother. Confucius said, "Give her one fu [about six dou]." Ran You asked for more. Confucius said, "Give her one yu [about sixteen dou]." Ran You then gave her five bing [about eighty-six hu]. Confucius remarked, "When Chi went to Qi, he rode on well-fed horses and wore light furs. I have heard that a noble person helps the destitute in their urgency, but does not add to the wealth of those who are already rich." Later, when Yuan Si was appointed steward of Confucius's household, Confucius gave him nine hundred measures of grain. Yuan Si declined. Confucius said, "Do not refuse it! Give the surplus to your neighbors and fellow villagers!"
meaning_notes: From the Analects, Book Yong Ye (雍也), headed "六之三." This passage illustrates Confucius's principle of 周急不繼富 — relieving urgent poverty rather than enriching the already comfortable. It also shows Confucius's personal generosity to Yuan Si when he declined the stipend. Key ancient grain units: 釜 (fǔ) ≈ 6 dou; 庾 (yǔ) ≈ 16 dou; 秉 (bǐng) ≈ 160 dou (or 5 bing ≈ 86 hu). 赤 (Chì) refers to Gongxi Chi (公西赤), courtesy name Zihua (子華). 原思 (Yuan Si) was Confucius's disciple Yuan Xian (原憲).
